```
Core value: "Tool descriptions tell an agent what a tool does, not how to orchestrate multiple tools together to achieve a goal."
Use MCP distribution when: skills tightly coupled to server tools, dynamic updates needed, different users need different content, cross-server orchestration, ephemeral availability, runtime-context-adaptive content.
Simpler alternatives suffice when: standalone skills, single-user single-machine, static files, existing infrastructure works.
```

### [7] Experimental Findings

**URL:** <https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/experimental-ext-skills/blob/main/docs/experimental-findings.md>

**Claims Made in Research:**
- McpGraph (875+ lines, Claude initially ignored skill)
- FastMCP 3.0 (pull model)
- NimbleBrain (skill:// consolidation)
- Model adherence is "time-decaying"
- Server instructions and subagent wrapping as workarounds

**Source Content (Pre-fetched):**
```
McpGraph: 875+ line SKILL.md. Claude initially ignored skill despite similar descriptions. Adding server instruction to read SKILL.md first resolved issue.
FastMCP 3.0: added skills support using pull model (vs push model with subscriptions).
NimbleBrain: consolidated separate repos into atomic repos with skills as skill:// resources. Same or better results.
Problem: models do not reliably load or follow skill instructions even when preloaded. Adherence is time-decaying.
Workarounds: server instructions, subagent wrapping, explicit discovery.
```

**Grade:** VERIFIED

**Evidence:** All claims directly match source content. "Time-decaying" is the exact terminology from the source.

### [12] Agent Skills Specification

**URL:** <https://agentskills.io/specification>

**Claims Made in Research:**
- SKILL.md format
- name (1-64 chars, lowercase+hyphens, must match parent dir)
- description (1-1024 chars)
- Optional license/compatibility/metadata/allowed-tools
- Progressive disclosure: ~100 tokens metadata, <5000 tokens instructions, resources on demand
- Keep under 500 lines

**Source Content (Pre-fetched):**
```
Skill = directory with SKILL.md (required) + optional scripts/, references/, assets/.
Frontmatter fields: name (required, 1-64 chars, lowercase+hyphens, must match parent dir), description (required, 1-1024 chars), license (optional), compatibility (optional, 1-500 chars), metadata (optional, key-value map), allowed-tools (optional, space-separated, experimental).
Progressive disclosure: metadata ~100 tokens at startup, instructions <5000 tokens on activation, resources loaded on demand.
Keep SKILL.md under 500 lines.
```

**Grade:** VERIFIED

**Evidence:** All length constraints match exactly (1-64, 1-1024, 500 lines, <5000 tokens, ~100 tokens). Directory structure requirement matches.

**Source Content (Pre-fetched):**
```
Converts any public GitHub repo with SKILL.md files into an MCP server.
Implements SEP-2640: each skill at skill://<name>/SKILL.md with enumerable skill://index.json.
Backward compat: every SKILL.md also wrapped as one MCP tool (frontmatter = schema, body = description).
Stable endpoints: https://mcp.skillsovermcp.com/mcp/<owner>/<repo>.
Changes propagate on push to main.
```

**Grade:** VERIFIED

**Evidence:** All claims match. The "tool-wrapper shim" is described in the source as backward-compatible tool wrapping.

Before finalizing, examining VERIFIED claims for over-claiming:

1. **"26+ platform adoption"** — The source [15] names specific platforms (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor, VS Code, ChatGPT, "20+ more"). The research does note this caveat in analysis.md. Grade remains VERIFIED because the claim is accurately attributed to the working group's findings, not presented as independently confirmed fact.

3. **"SEP-2640 In Review"** — Source [13] confirms this status as of the charter page. However, charters can be stale. The research does not claim acceptance, only that the proposal is In Review as documented. Grade remains VERIFIED.

4. **"No MCP client ships native skill:// support yet"** — This is stated in analysis.md and implementation-status.md. Source [14] confirms skillsovermcp.com uses a "tool-wrapper shim" specifically because "not every MCP client speaks skill:// yet." This is evidence of absence as of the source date. Cannot verify global absence, but the claim is appropriately scoped. Grade remains VERIFIED.
